title.narrative: Dominican Republic DRM Development Policy Loan with a Cat DDO

description.narrative: Project Development Objective The development objective of the proposed operation is to support the Government of the Dominican Republic in (a) strengthening institutions for improved climate and disaster resilience in priority sectors and (b) establishing mandatory regulations for climate and disaster risk reduction in public investment and construction works.

The development objective of the Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan with a Deferred Drawdown Option for Catastrophe Risks Project for Dominican Republic is to support the Government of the Dominican Republic in: (a) strengthening institutions for improved climate and disaster resilience in priority sectors; and (b) establishing mandatory regulations for climate and disaster risk reduction in public investment and construction works. The program has two pillars: Pillar A - Strengthening institutions for improved climate and disaster resilience in priority sectors; and Pillar B - Establishing mandatory regulations for climate and disaster risk reduction in public investment and construction works. The policy reforms supported by the proposed operation ensure the sustainability of the Government's efforts and commitment to a holistic approach to disaster risk reduction based on accountability and international best practices adapted to the context of the Dominican Republic.

title.narrative: Number of risk-prone areas in main watershed basins that have been prioritized, by hydrological and hydrometeorological studies, to undergo improvements in water management

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>(<em>Baseline [2016]: Studies have been conducted in 10 out of the 140 identified risk-prone areas - 7% of total </em></strong></p>

<p><strong><em>Target [2020]: Studies have been conducted in 50 out of the 140 identified risk-prone areas - 35% of total</em></strong><strong>)</strong></p>

<p>Of the 140 areas identified, only 23 have been studied or intervened by the Ministry of the Environment and Natural Resources - 50 areas studied being the objective. This indicator was affected by (i) institutional changes, (ii) lack of resources from the Ministry of the Environment, through the Climate Risk Management Commission to carry out the 27 studies that were pending, and (iii) the COVID crisis that affected the progress of the studies, including field visits. The target is deemed partially achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage (%) of public schools with a disaster risk assessment which are included in a rehabilitation and retrofitting program

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>(<em>Baseline [2016]: 0</em></strong></p>

<p><strong><em>Target [2020]: 30% of the schools assessed and requiring an intervention are rehabilitated and/or retrofitted</em></strong><strong>)</strong></p>

<p>The final reported number of educational centers with risk assessment and whose rehabilitation is in the due programming process is 82. MINERD reported in a communication dated August 20, 2021, that only 37 of the 470 schools previously reported, for which rehabilitation and maintenance works were programmed in 2018, and 45 of the 220 programmed in 2020, effectively benefited from a risk assessment by the General Directorate of Environmental and Risk Management (DIGAR) of MINERD. This was a substantial setback in the progression of the indicator representing roughly 12% of the goal of 30% of public schools with a disaster risk assessment included in a rehabilitation and modernization program. This setback is due in part to the important institutional changes that MINERD has been undertaking during 2019, with the change of minister, as well as the integration of the General Directorate of Rehabilitation (DIGRE) into the General Directorate of Infrastructure Maintenance School (DGMIE). It was also acknowledged by MINERD that there were discrepancies in the data initially reported.As a result, the Bank concludes that the target is only partially achieved. However, the Bank recognizes the significant efforts made by DIGAR despite its limited capacity to meet this target. The Bank also observes that, as a result of both the Program and the Technical Assistance to Integrate Disaster Risk Management in the Dominican Republic's School Infrastructure, MINERD's ability to understand and assess disaster risks in school infrastructure has significantly increased since 2017.</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Contingent liabilities associated with disasters are published and incorporated in the medium-term fiscal framework published by the Ministry of Finance

comment.narrative:
<p><strong><em>(Baseline [2016]: Does not exist</em></strong></p>

<p><strong><em><strong><em>Target [2020]: Document is published at least since 2019</em></strong></em></strong></p>

<p>Contingent liabilities associated with disasters were incorporated in the medium-term fiscal framework for 2019-2023 and 2020-2024. A fiscal risk report including an analysis of contingent liabilities related to disasters has been systematically annexed in the annual budget law which has been published every year since 2019. The target is deemed achieved.</p>
